issues.body: For every non-markdown form element, GitHub requires an `id` with a constrained format, and IDs must be unique within the form. `_assert_issue_form_valid` never inspects `id`, so an input/textarea/dropdown/checkboxes element with no ID, an invalid ID, or a duplicate ID passes this gate despite not satisfying the renderer schema. The truthiness-only `attributes.get(required)` checks have the same problem for types and nested shape: for example, `label: [x]`, `options: text`, or checkbox options without per-option `label` values are truthy and accepted even though they are not valid renderer shapes. The added tests only mutate body presence, name, element type, and one top-level required attribute, so none turns red for these omissions. This contradicts the marquee claim that touched forms are held to the shape GitHub's renderer requires and leaves a silent non-rendering path.
issues.fix_hint: Validate required non-markdown IDs (type, allowed syntax, and uniqueness), validate required attributes by their renderer-required types, and validate the nested option schema for dropdowns/checkboxes. Add focused negative fixtures for at least a missing/invalid/duplicate ID, wrong attribute types, and a checkbox option missing its label, while retaining a positive fixture for every supported element type.
issues.title: Validator accepts renderer-invalid element IDs and attribute shapes

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The new classification and fail-closed gate wiring are sound, but the validator does not actually enforce the renderer-required issue-form shape it claims to enforce. It accepts multiple syntactically valid forms that GitHub cannot render, and the self-tests omit those cases. Because this leaves the mint-path gap only partially closed, changes are required.
